title: Hosted API — Location locking, route policy & automated evidence orchestration
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Background:
Customers handling regulated data increasingly require both a declarative 'location lock' for tenant traffic and a dependable evidence trail proving the request routing and retention posture. Current Hosted API allows model routing and region hints, but there is no tenant-level enforcement boundary nor a first-class evidence package that ties routing events to retention records for audits.

Goal:
Deliver a combined UX + API + evidence orchestration feature we call 'Location Locking' that: (1) lets operators pin a tenant to an allowed set of physical regions with a strict enforcement mode, (2) surfaces routing decisions and fallbacks in Console, (3) automates generation of time-bounded evidence bundles (routing trace, retention policy snapshot, KMS key IDs, and transfer logs) suitable for customer audits.

Scope / Non-goals:
- In scope: Hosted API tenant config, Console controls for lock mode and allowed regions, enforcement behavior for strict/soft modes, auto evidence package generation, retention snapshot export, operator override audit log, SLOs for evidence availability.
- Out of scope: Private/VPC control plane changes, on-prem runtime upgrades, billing/reserved-capacity accounting changes (follow-up ticket).

Proposed solution (high level):
1) Tenant config API: add /v1/tenants/{id}/location-lock with fields: mode=(strict|soft|off), allowed_regions=[...], evidence_retention_days, operator_contact. Strict mode rejects requests that cannot be routed to allowed_regions; soft mode routes but annotates and flags for review.
2) Runtime enforcement: smart-routing layer evaluates tenant lock before routing. If strict and capacity unavailable in allowed set, fail fast with new 403_LocationLocked response and audit payload. If soft, route to best region and annotate with deviation_reason.
3) Evidence pipeline: when any routing decision occurs for a locked tenant, stream a compact event into evidence-service which composes a signed bundle hourly and on any deviation. Bundle contains: request IDs, chosen region, policy snapshot (tenant config hash), retention profile, KMS key fingerprint used for any stored artifacts, and a checksum manifest. Bundles are versioned and stored in the tenant's evidence vault for N days per evidence_retention_days.
4) Console UX: new Location Lock page under Tenant Settings showing current mode, allowed regions, last 24h routing map, last evidence bundle time, and operator override history. Include a "Simulate" button for admins to test traffic scenarios and expected enforcement result.
5) APIs for evidence export: /v1/tenants/{id}/evidence?from=...&to=... returns signed bundle links and an integrity checksum.

Acceptance criteria:
- PM + Security signoff on policy/manifest format and proof signature scheme.
- Tenant config API available in beta for self-service tenants.
- Runtime rejects strict-mode disallowed flows with documented error codes and emits evidence events for every rejection.
- Console page shows routing map and allows simulation.
- Evidence bundles available for download and match acceptance manifest schema.

Engineering notes and trade-offs:
- We recommend a compact hourly bundling approach (vs per-request) to limit storage and signer throughput; bundling must still include per-request identifiers to make bundles auditable.
- Strict mode availability: rejecting requests will create customer-visible errors and could be high-impact for tenants without reserved capacity. We need to default new tenants to soft mode.
- Signed bundles use existing infra signing keyring; security prefers HSM-backed signatures but initial MVP will use KMS-signed S3 objects.

Design and UX feedback so far (from review 2026-03-05):
- Designers asked for a simple toggle for strict vs soft, but with a clear inline warning about SLA/customer impact.
- Add a "where-will-my-data-go" map for common origin regions to set expectations.
- Simulation flow must show a sample request path, fallback reason, and a preview of the evidence bundle entry.

Open questions / blockers:
- How to represent multi-region legal constructs (e.g., EEA vs EU27 vs specific countries)? Need taxonomy decision from Legal.
- Do we need per-route overrides vs per-tenant only? Engineering prefers per-tenant first to limit complexity.
- Evidence retention legal minimums vary by geography; we need product/legal guidance for defaults.

Implementation plan / milestones:
- Week 1 (2026-W10): API schema + Console wireframes (PM + Design).
- Week 2-3: Runtime gating logic + evidence event schema (ENG).
- Week 4: Evidence bundle composer + signed storage (ENG + Security).
- Week 5: Console implementation + simulate button + end-to-end tests (PM/Design/QA).
- Week 6: Beta rollout to pilot tenants and collect fallout metrics.

Rollout strategy and risk mitigation:
- Start defaulting new tenants to soft mode only. Strict mode must require an online acknowledgment and a warning about potential 403 failures.
- Offer a migration guide for tenants to reserve Dedicated capacity if they require strict enforcement with guaranteed throughput.
- Provide dashboards to monitor number of soft deviations and strict rejections per tenant per hour; target to keep incidents under a low threshold before enabling strict mode for larger tenants.

Testing plan / QA checklist:
- Unit tests for policy evaluation logic and error responses.
- Integration tests simulating capacity shortfalls across regions verifying strict vs soft behavior.
- End-to-end validation that evidence bundles include all required fields and signature verifies with configured KMS keys.
- UX QA validating simulate flow accuracy and operator override audit entries.

Follow-ups / future work (not in MVP):
- Operator automation: auto-retry into alternate allowed region sets and automated remediation playbooks.
- Per-route overrides for function-level pinning and pbk routing.
- Cross-tenant aggregated evidence analytics for internal compliance reporting.

Decision log (so far):
- Use soft-by-default to reduce customer outages (decision 2026-03-03).
- Use hourly bundling with event-level identifiers to balance auditability vs cost (decision 2026-03-04).
- Use KMS-signed S3 storage for MVP evidence bundles; HSM planned later (decision 2026-03-06).

Acceptance tests / sample scenarios to run in pilot:
- Tenant A (soft mode) triggers a deviation during a regional outage: request succeeds, evidence bundle records deviation, console flags tenant for review.
- Tenant B (strict mode) non-resident request receives 403_LocationLocked and an evidence bundle is immediately generated with rejection details.
- Simulation scenarios accurately reflect the runtime decision tree and produce previewed evidence entries.

Notes and links to artifacts: see linked PR and designs.

Next steps for assignee (Liam Chen):
- Finalize API schema and post to Confluence by 2026-03-16.
- Coordinate security review request and KMS key access patterns by 2026-03-20.
- Schedule pilot tenants and prepare a short release notes draft for hosted-2026.04.
